reason: The main claim in part (1) is wrong. The API does expose finals ticks. kagglesdk competition_enums.py l.59-63 defines SubmissionGroup.SUBMISSION_GROUP_SELECTED = 2, and in kaggle 2.2.4 KaggleApi.competition_submissions(competition, group=...) passes it through ApiListSubmissionsRequest.group. A read-only call at ~08:32Z returned 0 with group=SELECTED and 40 with group=ALL. A read-only Chrome check of the Submissions page at ~08:34Z showed the heading '0/2', so the API and the web page agree. ApiSubmission has no 'selected' field, but the SELECTED filter makes one unnecessary. Part (2) is correct: ApiKernelMetadata has no score field, so the kernel CLI can only detect changes. The practical point of the finding holds, and is more urgent than stated: the finals are NOT ticked now. If they stay unticked, Kaggle auto-selects by public score, and three files tie at 0.954: #37, #35 (R5-unproven) and P36 (diagnostic). The auto-pick could therefore land on P36 + #35, which the finals rule forbids. The value is real (finals hygiene, no LB or lab artefact), with no runtime or rule impact.
fix: Now: ask the user to tick #37 (56563521, 'probe 37: exp58') and #38 (56563534, 'probe 38: exp58n'). The page shows 0/2 as of ~08:34Z. After the tick, verify it with the CLI: python -c "from kaggle.api.kaggle_api_extended import KaggleApi; from kagglesdk.competitions.types.competition_enums import SubmissionGroup as G; a=KaggleApi(); a.authenticate(); print([s.ref for s in a.competition_submissions('biohub-cell-tracking-during-development', group=G.SUBMISSION_GROUP_SELECTED)])". It must print exactly {56563521, 56563534}. Do one browser read or a user screenshot too, the first time only, to confirm the filter returns positives. Then log 'FINALS TICKED 2/2: 56563521 + 56563534 (seen hh:mmZ, API+page)' in CONTEXT. Optionally add the SELECTED check to the lb_poll cycle and alert when the set is not {56563521, 56563534}. Run it again on 28 Sep evening and 29 Sep 12:00/18:00. For E10, keep part (2) as is: a CLI change detector on the top-10 refs by scoreDescending and by dateRun, plus the LB histogram, and open the browser only when something changes.
realistic_gain: No LB gain. It prevents a finals-selection accident: without a tick Kaggle could auto-pick P36 or #35 from the 0.954 tie. It also makes the tick check scriptable, so it can run in the poller at no cost instead of through manual browser reads on 28 and 29 Sep.
